title: Bigger models, bigger valuations, and Washington's mixed signals
body:
This month the index tilted toward a few powerful owners holding very capable AI. Enslaved God, the 'genie in a box' ending, stayed on top and rose from 36.4 to 40.3. Zookeeper (+3.9), Protector God (+3.8), Descendants (+3.8) and Benevolent Dictator (+3.8) also gained, while Libertarian Utopia (-1.2), Reversion (-0.9) and Egalitarian Utopia (-0.8) slipped. Horizon Balance ended at 1.8, a little below the 1.9 it started at, after dipping to 0.4 on 21 May and climbing to 2.5 on 4 June.

Capability drove much of it. Google I/O launched always-on agents, an OpenAI model disproved an Erdos conjecture checked by outside mathematicians, and Anthropic shipped Opus 4.8 and then Claude Fable 5. Money concentrated at the same time: the jury rejected Musk's case against OpenAI, Anthropic raised at about $900B and then filed for an IPO at $965B post-money, and SpaceX, owner of xAI, listed at about $1.75T.

Washington swung back and forth. Trump scrapped an AI testing order on 21 May, signed a scaled-back version on 2 June, and a bipartisan draft bill on 4 June would require frontier safety frameworks. Then on 12 June an emergency export-control directive forced Anthropic to shut down Fable 5 worldwide, sinking Gatekeeper by 1.5 in a day.

Across the month, Capability Velocity rose 3.5, Power Concentration 3.2, AI Autonomy 2.4, and Alignment & Control 1.2, while Global Coordination fell 1.4.
